meta.title: A Walk with Four Short Texts
meta.textType: parts of a notice, a caption, a blog post, and instructions

paragraphs: A Walk with Four Short Texts, posted by Lily. On Saturday, the Explorers will go on a photo walk. We will walk on the old town path and take pictures. The path is old, and the houses next to it are old too. Teacher Kim made four short texts for the walk. I will show them to you, and I will name the parts of each one. It is a good plan.

First, there is a notice in the school gallery. It is next to the library door. A notice is a note for many people, and it is on a wall. The title at the top says, "Photo Walk." Under the title, the message says, "We meet at the school gate at eight o'clock." The next line says, "Bring walking shoes and a bottle of water." Another line says, "Bring a badminton racket for a game after the walk." At the bottom, there is the name of the writer, Teacher Kim.

Second, here is a caption from my photo album. The photo shows Mia and May on the old town path. The caption says, "Mia and May walk on the old town path." I took the photo early, and the light was soft. A caption tells who is in the photo. It also tells where they are, and it has only a few words.

Third, here is a short blog post by May. The title is "I Love Walking," and the writer is May. In the middle, May writes, "I think walking is better than the bus." She also writes, "On a walk, you see many small things." The last line asks, "Where do you like to walk?" I agree with May, because I like to look at the shops and the trees. This post shows the opinion of May, and she gives a reason.

Last, here are the instructions for the map of the path. The title says, "How to Download the Map." Step one says, "Open the school page on a laptop." Step two says, "Click the link for the map." Step three says, "Click download, and wait." Step four says, "Open the file, and follow the directions." The directions show the way from the school gate to the park. The map is small, so it is easy to download. Instructions have steps in order, and each step starts with an action word.
Now you know the parts of four short texts. Which text helps you most on a walk?
